Incorporating the April 2023 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) sharpens the growth-cautious, hawkish read of the May 3 FOMC statement. The SLOOS shows broad and notable tightening in credit supply:
- C&I: Banks tightened standards and terms; cited the economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, deteriorating collateral values, higher funding costs, deposit outflows, and liquidity concerns. Loan demand weakened (plant/equipment, M&A, inventory, and A/R financing).
- CRE: Underwriting tightened materially with wider spreads, lower LTVs, and higher DSCRs across nonfarm nonresidential and multifamily.
- Consumer: Tighter standards/terms across autos, cards, HELOCs, and mortgages (QM and non-QM).
- Foreign and mid-sized banks also tightened, and banks expect further tightening ahead.

These SLOOS signals corroborate and amplify the FOMC’s warning that tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity and hiring, increasing the downside risks to growth and risk assets relative to a purely macro read. While policy backstops (e.g., BTFP and coordinated liquidity lines) help contain systemic tail risks, the near-term impulse from credit supply is more negative and likely persistent. Net: tilt more negative than the prior assessment.
